question: After realising the deadly effects of depleting the ozone layer, under which programme was the decision taken to ban the usage of CFC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Environment Programme**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The decision to ban the usage of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) was taken under the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**.
 
• UNEP is responsible for coordinating responses to environmental issues within the United Nations system.
 
• It was established in 1972 following the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm.
 
• The Montreal Protocol, an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances responsible for ozone depletion, was adopted under the auspices of UNEP.
 
• The Protocol has been successful in reducing the global production of CFCs and other ozone-depleting chemicals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Montreal Protocol** was signed on 16th September 1987 and came into effect on 1st January 1989.
 
• It is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date, with widespread global participation.
 
• Amendments to the Protocol have been made to include additional substances and to accelerate the phase-out schedules.
 
• The **Kigali Amendment**, adopted in 2016, aims to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are potent greenhouse gases.
 
• UNEP continues to play a crucial role in monitoring and supporting the implementation of the Montreal Protocol.
